How to play Eurovision Games in 60 seconds

A free, browser-based party game for the Eurovision Song Contest. Players predict the Top 5 and Worst 5, battle in head-to-head trivia duels, and chase five winner trophies — all while the show is on. No app, no account for guests, 2 to 20 players.

01

Setup in 60 seconds

One host creates the room — no sign-up, no email. Everyone else joins from a link. The whole flow from empty browser tab to locked-in predictions is a single minute.

  1. 1

    Create the room

    10s

    Click Create a Room, enter your name, pick an avatar and set a room password. A 6-character room code appears; the room holds up to 20 players.

  2. 2

    Invite friends

    20s

    Share the code, the join link and the room password (all included in the share message). Phone or laptop, any modern browser. When everyone’s in, tap Start the Party!

  3. 3

    Make predictions (before or during the show)

    Every player builds a Top 5 and Worst 5. Picks stay editable through the songs and lock automatically when voting opens.

  4. 4

    Trivia warm-up

    Each player plays 3 quiz rounds at their own pace, any time from party start until voting opens — points carry into the night total.

  5. 5

    Duel time

    Duels are open from party start too — challenge anyone in the room during postcards and ad breaks. Quiz, duels and predictions all lock automatically when voting opens.

  6. Voting live
    Predictions, quiz and duels lock automatically.
    6

    Trophy reveal

    When the official results are final, the room moves to Final Results automatically and five winners are crowned.

02

Trivia duels during the show

A duel is a 3-question Eurovision trivia battle between two players in the room. Questions fire on a 12-second timer; speed and accuracy both count.

How a duel plays out

Tap any other player’s name any time from party start until voting opens and choose Challenge. Both players answer the same 3 questions in private. The higher answer total wins the duel; equal totals are a tie. There is no win bonus — the winner picks Steal (move their duel score from the loser to themselves) or Double (add twice their duel score to themselves).

Each of you can challenge the other once, and the loser of a duel can request one rematch; once a rematch exists, that pair can’t duel again — so nobody grinds one opponent for points all night. Refusing costs no points, but refusals are limited: 2 per player in rooms of up to 5, 3 with 6–10, 4 with 11–15 and 5 with 16 or more (refused rematches count).

03

Lock predictions

Predictions are the bedrock of the night — they score automatically the moment Eurovision results come in, so they reward homework and a bit of nerve.

  • Top 5. The five countries you think will finish 1–5 in the official combined ranking, in your predicted order.
  • Worst 5. The five countries you think will finish bottom of the leaderboard, ordered last-place first.
  • No overlap. A country can appear in only one list per player.
  • Order matters. An exact-position hit pays 50 points; a country that lands in the right list at the wrong rank pays 20.
  • Hard lock. Predictions lock automatically when voting opens (Voting Live) — no edits after that. Late joiners can still enter predictions, play trivia and duel until then.

04

Live scoring

As Eurovision jury and televote results come in, predictions auto-score against the official combined ranking and the leaderboard updates instantly for everyone in the room.

  • Top 5 / Worst 5 score against the final combined ranking the moment results land.
  • Quiz points are banked as you answer and never change.
  • Duel points swing in real time as duels resolve through the broadcast.
  • No data entry — official jury and televote results are pulled in automatically on grand-final night; nobody has to type them in.
05

Five winner trophies

At the end of the night, five trophy cards are revealed in sequence:

  • Champion — most total points across every phase. The headline title.
  • Thief — most points stolen via duel Steal effects.
  • Duelist — most duels won across the night.
  • Oracle — highest prediction-only score (Top 5 + Worst 5 totals).
  • Guru — most correct answers across all quiz rounds (duel answers don’t count).

One player can win multiple trophies. Co-winners (2–5 tied) split a single trophy unless the room votes for sudden death.

06

Sudden-death tiebreak

For any tied trophy category, the host opens a 60-second tiebreak vote — the room chooses Accept (co-winners share the trophy) or Sudden Death. Sudden Death only goes ahead if it wins a clear majority with at least 3 votes cast. If it does, the tied players enter a 3-question trivia match; most correct answers wins — speed breaks ties. If the vote stays with Accept, all tied players share the trophy.

07

What you need

  • A modern browser. Chrome 120+, Safari 17+, Firefox 121+, Edge 120+ — phone or desktop. PWA install on iOS and Android.
  • 2 to 20 players. Couples can share a single device.
  • The Eurovision broadcast. TV, official stream, or the EBU’s YouTube live feed — anything that lets you watch in real time.
  • No payment, no install, no accounts. Not even the host signs up.
